title: A bilingual recap of the R&D project and its product, and keeping it current
request: Give me one document I can read or share about everything done so far: the vision, each round of work, where the repository stands, the real findings, the product demo, the roadmap and the open questions, with a Persian summary. Later the same day: this is the recap of what I did until now; update it and regenerate the PDF.
spec: docs/recap/recap.html as the source and docs/recap/DCLab_RD_Recap.pdf built from it, in English with a Persian summary. On update: every number and status checked against the repository today, and the PDF regenerated and checked page by page.
plan: Write the recap from the repository's own records: the vision, every round of work in order, the state of the repository, the measured findings, the demo, the roadmap and the open questions; add a Persian summary; render the PDF.
When asked to update it, read the whole recap and compare it with the repository before editing.
Report the parts that are out of date and ask before rewriting.
Refresh the numbers (latest commit, test count, failing tests, whether any blueprint decisions were saved) from the repository itself.
Add the new rounds of work, mark the fixed bug as fixed with its re-check numbers, update the demo section, and add a Persian walkthrough of the demo.
Regenerate the PDF and check every page by eye; fix page breaks that leave a note alone on a page.

decisions.decision: Every number in the recap is read from the repository at the time of writing, not copied from the old recap.
decisions.why: A recap that repeats stale numbers misleads the people it is shared with.

decisions.decision: The out-of-date parts were listed first and the rewrite waited for the owner's yes.
decisions.why: The owner had only shared the recap; changing a shared document is the owner's call.

decisions.decision: Failing tests are reported in the recap with their known cause, not hidden.
decisions.why: The recap is a status document; one test failed because of another session's unfinished work, which a reader needs to know.

decisions.decision: Uncommitted changes from another session were left untouched.
decisions.why: The working copy held another session's work in progress; only the recap belonged to this task.

change: Commit 9ddc401 added docs/recap/recap.html and DCLab_RD_Recap.pdf. The later update (left uncommitted at the owner's choice) moved the latest commit and date, added two rounds (the category-code fix and the demo redesign), refreshed the test numbers, marked the category-code bug fixed with its re-check result, rewrote the demo section for the new sidebar groups and the Overview plus tabs layout, updated the Persian summary, added a Persian section-by-section walkthrough of the demo, and removed page breaks that left short notes alone on a page. The PDF is 10 pages.

findings.defect: The shared recap was out of date in three places a day after it was written.
findings.scenario: The demo section still listed the old page groups after the redesign; the category-code bug was still listed as open although its fix was committed; the test section said 94 tests pass while the suite then ran more tests and one failed.
findings.cause: A recap is a snapshot; the repository kept moving.
findings.fix: Compare the recap with the repository before every update and refresh each number from its source.
findings.test: Checked against make rd-check output and git log at the time of the update.

findings.defect: The regenerated PDF had a short note alone on its own page.
findings.scenario: After the new sections were added, the 'Open it' note was pushed onto a page of its own by a forced page break.
findings.cause: A fixed page break written for the earlier length of the document.
findings.fix: Remove the page break and regenerate the PDF.
findings.test: Every page of the PDF checked by eye.

outcome: Done: a bilingual recap the owner can share, and an update that brought it in line with the repository on 5 October, including a Persian walkthrough of the demo.
lessons: A status document is only as good as its last check against the source; refresh every number from where it lives.
Fixed page breaks break when content grows; check a regenerated PDF page by page.
